chapter_note: Heavily damaged chapter (84%) but the surviving content is a clear correspondential teaching mapping the production of speech (mouth, tongue, teeth, lips, members) onto the five artisans who form and adorn a coin (engraving, cutting, sealing, forging the blank). Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic/natural system — speech-organs ↔ five artisans of coinage ↔ word coming forth. This is classic substrate correspondence. Editorial overlay is minimal: only the formulaic 'Once again he said' attribution and the bare 'He said' need stripping. The high apostolic_dialogue scores in i=3, i=5 are picking up exactly these formulae.
